newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares off at noon on Bengang slide.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares off at noon on Bengang slide.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index was easier at midday on Tuesday, pulled lower by weakness in market newcomer Bengang Steel, brokers said.
The index lost 0.44 point or 0.34 percent to 129.59 on thin turnover of HK$9.5 million.
B shares fell despite a modest rise in the domestic A share index, which was up 3.35 points or 0.85 percent to 397.82 on turnover of 1.97 billion yuan.
"The fall in the B share index was mainly due to Bengang," said an analyst at China Guotai Securities. "The poor performance of Bengang's shares has dented investor confidence."

Bengang shed HK$0.04 to HK$1.99 on volume of 1.4 million shares, making it the most active issue. The company listed 400 million B shares earlier this month and the stock has moved well below its offer price of HK$2.38.
Brokers have blamed Bengang's falls on investor pessimism over China's steel sector.
But B shares could gain some support from any steadying of the A share market, brokers said.
"If A shares can stabilise, the B share index probably can hold above the 130-point level," the Guotai analyst said.
Beverage maker Shenbao Industrial was the biggest B share loser, tumbling HK$0.30 or 9.09 percent to HK$3.00.
On the A share market, Shenzhen Development Bank was among the session's most actively traded stocks, rebounding 0.47 yuan to 34.05 yuan on volume of 4.2 million shares.
